main_body: Two timber-framed gabled houses joined by a connecting wall, with large tiled roofs above half-timbered plaster walls and a front door
top_band: Orange and gold roof tiles with highlight rows, from about row 0 to row 37 in the centre column, then the gable triangle and the timber beam at about row 47
evidence: The tall tiled roof is a large sloped surface seen from above, lit lighter than the walls. A dark timber beam marks the eave line, with a shadow band on the plaster just below it. The south wall below is a distinct vertical face with timber framing, grey ledge bands, a window with a sill box and a plank door. The hip roof wings on the sides also show their slopes. This matches the reference houses, so it reads as a correct 3/4 building.

style.evidence: The roof tiles carry per-tile highlights across about five tone steps (gold, orange, mid, magenta-brown, deep), the same craft as the reference. Outlines and beams are dark brown, a tinted wood tone, not black. The plaster has speckle dots and the door has grain and studs. The windows have shading and the flower boxes add colour variety. Tiles hold many colours, at least as dense as the references, and no large area is a flat fill.
